content:
MODEL CHARTER — CURRENT
The Retail Credit Default Model is used to estimate 12-month probability of default for unsecured retail loans. Approved model version 3.0 is owned by Marcus Lee in Consumer Lending Risk. It is classified Tier 1. The current operating decision threshold is 0.58. This charter supersedes RCD-CHR-v1 effective 2025-10-01. Required control: quarterly performance monitoring and annual independent validation.

DEVELOPMENT REPORT
Purpose: estimate 12-month probability of default for unsecured retail loans. Development data consist of anonymized application, bureau, and 12-month repayment snapshots from 2021-2024. Records were de-identified or synthetic before modeling. Time-based sampling was used: earlier observations for development and later observations for holdout testing. The report documents transformations, missing-value rules, feature definitions, and reproducible code parameters. Known limitation: thin-file applicants are underrepresented in the development sample. No customer names, account numbers, or raw protected-attribute values are retained in this benchmark record.

INDEPENDENT VALIDATION — SUPERSEDED
Validation of version 2.3 reported area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.781. Testing covered conceptual soundness, implementation verification, sensitivity analysis, and outcomes analysis. The principal limitation was that thin-file applicants are underrepresented in the development sample. This validation was superseded by RCD-VAL-v2 on 2025-11-15.

INDEPENDENT VALIDATION — CURRENT
Validation of approved version 3.0 reported area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.804. Independent testing covered conceptual soundness, implementation verification, sensitivity analysis, outcomes analysis, and review of use. The remaining limitation is that thin-file applicants are underrepresented in the development sample. Validation approved use subject to quarterly performance monitoring and annual independent validation. This report supersedes RCD-VAL-v1.

2026 Q1 MONITORING
Observed area under the ROC curve (AUC): 0.792. The control limit is AUC below 0.760. Q1 status: within tolerance. No escalation was required. Monitoring used the approved production population and documented segment checks.

2026 Q2 MONITORING
Observed area under the ROC curve (AUC): 0.751. The control limit is AUC below 0.760. Q2 status: breached. The identified issue was Q2 AUC deterioration for thin-file applicants. Issue ISS-RCD-2026-01 was opened for remediation and governance review.

ISSUE LOG SNAPSHOT
Issue ID: ISS-RCD-2026-01. Finding: Q2 AUC deterioration for thin-file applicants. Severity: moderate. Status as of 2026-07-05: OPEN. Target completion date: 2026-08-31. The assigned owner is Marcus Lee. Closure requires remediation evidence and Model Risk Committee confirmation.

REMEDIATION EVIDENCE
Issue ID: ISS-RCD-2026-01. The model team introduced a thin-file monitoring segment and a conservative manual-review overlay. Control testing on 2026-08-18 found the change implemented as designed. Management requested closure, but final closure remained subject to Model Risk Committee confirmation.

MODEL RISK COMMITTEE MINUTES
The committee confirmed model version 3.0 and current threshold 0.58. It reviewed remediation for ISS-RCD-2026-01: introduced a thin-file monitoring segment and a conservative manual-review overlay. Based on successful control testing, the committee CLOSED ISS-RCD-2026-01 effective 2026-09-01. Continued use was approved subject to quarterly performance monitoring and annual independent validation.

POLICY CONTROL MAPPING
The Retail Credit Default Model is Tier 1 and is subject to a risk-based governance approach. Accountable business unit: Consumer Lending Risk. Required control: quarterly performance monitoring and annual independent validation. Independent validation must remain separate from model ownership. Governance mapping references the 2026 revised interagency model-risk guidance and NIST AI RMF for general AI governance. Generative AI is governed by bank policy even though the 2026 banking guidance states that generative and agentic AI are outside that guidance's scope.

DATA QUALITY REPORT
The governed source is anonymized application, bureau, and 12-month repayment snapshots from 2021-2024. Automated checks covered schema conformity, missingness, duplicates, valid ranges, and reconciliation totals. Q2 controls passed except for the known representation limitation: thin-file applicants are underrepresented in the development sample. The report contains aggregate quality results only. It does not contain customer names, account numbers, protected-attribute values, or vendor source code.
